title: Streaming schema contracts, graceful fallback, and error-handling acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD fragment and acceptance criteria for how Redwood services must produce, validate, and fallback for streamed structured outputs when invoking external tools or internal function-calls. Scope covers schema negotiation, progressive JSON emission, error modes (soft/hard failures), partial-result checkpointing, resume semantics, and canary rollout gating. This ticket clarifies requirements and provides test vectors for engineering and design to implement and validate behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation: model responses must include a top-level metadata token at stream start that declares the output schema version (e.g., "schema_v": "1.1") or the response will be treated as unstructured and routed to fallback flow.

Progressive JSON: the stream must emit valid incremental JSON pieces that can be reassembled into a final JSON document without external heuristics; partial objects are allowed but must be clearly delimited as `progress_chunk` entries in the stream metadata.
Tool-call envelope: every tool/function invocation event in the stream must include an invocation id, tool name, expected output schema id, and an optional checksum for payload integrity.

Validation window: the system must validate the assembled JSON against the declared schema within 200ms of stream end; schema violations trigger deterministic fallback policies (see fallback behaviors).

Fallback behaviors: defined deterministic order - (1) attempt structured-cleanup transform (auto-fix common issues), (2) retry the tool invocation with `strict_schema=true` up to 1 retry, (3) return best-effort unstructured text with diagnostic metadata and `tool_status: degraded`. Each fallback step must be logged and surfaced to the user via the console with an error code.

Streaming error signaling: stream-level errors must use a stable set of error codes (e.g., SERR-1001 for transient network, SERR-2002 for schema-mismatch) and include human-readable message and optional recovery_hint field.

Partial result availability: consumers must be able to read and use partial structured results (e.g., first 80% of rows) with an explicit `partial: true` flag; partial outputs must be accompanied by `estimated_completion` timestamp when available.

Resume semantics: for private/dedicated deployments where long-lived connections may drop, the client may resume a stream using the invocation id within 60 seconds; the service must support resumption by replaying the remaining tokens from a persisted checkpoint if available.

Security: any tool payload signed by a customer key must surface signature verification status in the stream metadata; failed signature verification must take the `strict` fallback path rather than best-effort output.
Observability: each streamed invocation must emit token-level latency histogram samples and per-invocation CPU/GPU usage summary to the console within 1 minute of completion for paid environments.
Backward compatibility: when schema version is missing, behavior must match legacy `unstructured` mode and be explicitly labeled; no silent schema coercions are allowed for GA release.
Canary gating: rollout must block GA if more than 5% of canary invocations for a schema-version result in `schema_mismatch` or `SERR-3XXX` class errors over a 24h window.
test_cases: TC-01: Streamed successful tool-call producing large JSON array (10k items); final payload validates against schema_v=1.1 and no fallback is used.
TC-02: Stream emits interleaved text and progress_chunk entries; assembly must preserve intended structure and validate.
TC-03: Simulate 1 network disconnect and resume within 30s; resumed stream must continue from last checkpoint without duplicate objects.
TC-04: Schema mismatch: model emits integer for field declared as string. System must attempt auto-cleanup, then retry with strict_schema, then return degraded unstructured output with diagnostics.
TC-05: Tool returns payload with altered checksum; service must detect integrity failure and route to strict fallback with an audit log link.
TC-06: High-latency scenario: token emission stalls for 8s; stream should emit heartbeat metadata and not be treated as failed if stall < 15s.
TC-07: Security test: signed payload with invalid signature must be rejected in strict mode and surfaced as SERR-5001 signature_failure.
TC-08: Canary test: run 500 invocations across dedicated region; verify error rate during canary stays below 5% for 24h.
design_notes: Design decision: prefer explicit metadata handshake over heuristic schema detection to reduce silent failures and improve observability.
Trade-off: requiring schema metadata at stream-start increases client integration complexity for quick experiments but enables deterministic validation and instrumentation.
UX: Console should surface a compact stream replay view with markers for fallback events and retry attempts.
Accessibility: partial results shown in the console must indicate their `partial` status visually and via an aria-label for screen readers.
engineering_notes: Implementation hint: persist per-invocation checkpoints to the existing KV cache with TTL=120s to support resume semantics in private deployments.
Performance: validation step must be I/O non-blocking; consider streaming JSON schema validators or incremental validation to keep validation latency <200ms.
Backwards-compat: add a feature flag `require_stream_schema_v1` behind canary to flip behavior for early adopters.
Dependencies: requires updates to runtime streaming protocol, console stream visualizer, and metrics exporter. See dependency keys.
change_log: 2026-02-25: created by Sofia Martinez — initial scope and acceptance list.
2026-03-02: added resume semantics after engineering spike — Ethan Zhou.
2026-03-07: widened fallback policy to include auto-cleanup transform — review with Reliability.
2026-03-14: updated canary gating thresholds and observability requirements after security review.
review_feedback: Reliability: need clearer SLOs for stream completion vs partial availability — assigned to ENG for proposal.
Security: add KMS-signed payload test vectors for private deploys — requested by Security team.
Design: console replay should include a compact diff view for each retry to help debugging — design to provide mockups.
PM: consider softer default fallback (best-effort + warning) for low-tier hosted customers to reduce noisy failures.
risks: Risk: strict validation may increase apparent error rates for customers with older prompts — mitigated by canary and soft-fallback flow.
Risk: checkpointing increases storage/IO pressure on runtime — mitigated by short TTL and sampling for observability.
Risk: additional metadata increases token overhead for high-volume workloads — mitigation plan includes compact binary-encoded metadata in Dedicated later.
